A JSON Merge Patch of a subscription (RFC 7386): the spend cap and the alert percent.

`forbid`: any other member is a 422, not a silent no-op. A member left out stays as it is.
`null` removes the cap, and a removed cap is no cap: so `null` here has one meaning only.
The alert percent always has a value, so `null` for it is a 422.

auto_reload.description: Fill the balance by itself: when it falls below `threshold`, keelie charges the Consumer's saved card for one `pack`. It needs a card saved by a top-up with `save_for_auto_top_up`, and a spend limit (`spend_cap` or the plan's `cost_ceiling`), with room for `threshold` plus `pack`. keelie buys at most the spend limit in credits each month, and stops when the Consumer's burn this month reaches the limit. Each change records `consent_ref` and the time again, and sets `auto_reload_state` back to `ok` after a failed charge. `null` turns it off.

spend_cap.description: The Consumer's own limit, which the Provider sets for them: the most credits they may burn in a UTC calendar month. At it, their next token is refused. `"0"` refuses every token. The plan's `cost_ceiling` applies when it is lower. `null` removes the cap. It stops spending and bills nothing.

tags.description: Liveness. Public: it needs no credential.
tags.name: Status

tags.description: Providers. Signup is public, because nobody holds a credential before it. Everything else about an org needs one.
tags.name: Orgs

tags.description: What a Provider sells. Registering one takes a URL: keelie fetches the document there and reads every route out of it, so the Provider writes nothing else.
tags.name: Products

tags.description: What a Consumer pays the Provider. One mechanism: a fee, an included quantity, and the packs that fill the balance again. A plan with the fee and the quantity at zero is a balance-only plan, not a second kind of plan.
tags.name: Plans

tags.description: The Provider's customers. A Consumer subscribes to plans and holds credentials. keelie keeps a name and the Provider's own reference, and no person's data.
tags.name: Consumers

tags.description: One Consumer on one published plan version. The subscription holds the plan's scopes, and every credential issued on it carries them.
tags.name: Subscriptions

tags.description: A Consumer's client id and client secret, issued on a subscription. The secret is shown once. A revoked credential mints no new token; a token minted before lives until it expires.
tags.name: Credentials

tags.description: The Provider's AI Catalog (ai-catalog.io): what an agent reads to choose an API. keelie builds it on each read from the published plans, so it never disagrees with them. The SDK serves it on the Provider's own domain, at `/.well-known/ard.json` and `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`.
tags.name: Catalog

tags.description: What the Provider's SDK reports about each call. It feeds the Provider's dashboards and the Consumer's balance. Apiable never bills on it.
tags.name: Usage

tags.description: Where keelie tells the Provider what happened: a spend alert, a subscription made or changed, a credential revoked. Each message is signed per Standard Webhooks, and a failed delivery is tried again for about three days. A notification, never a bill.
tags.name: Webhooks
